subject: Residency safeguard operations: narrow temporary egress examples and acceptance questions
messages:
From: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal - Acme Health <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Residency assurances for pilot and temporary-egress examples

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're preparing our procurement package and need a short note on how Redwood will handle: (1) strict EU residency for production PII, and (2) any temporary cross-region processing during failover/burst scenarios for the pilot (non-production sandbox traffic).

Specifically can you confirm:
- Which subprocessors may process data during a temporary failover?
- Maximum length for transient cross-border processing in hours (e.g., caching, KV-syncs, logging) you expect to allow for pilot customers?
- Evidence we can include in our DPA submission (SOC2 control points, sample audit logs, subprocessor roster).

Attached: Acme_DPA_Redlines.pdf (initial redlines from Legal). We appreciate a concise operational example we can present to our privacy/compliance team.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
DPO, Acme Health

---
Acme Health (external)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency assurances for pilot and temporary-egress examples

Priya — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and an operational playbook attached for the pilot. I'm looping in Marissa (account lead) and Kimberly (legal) to confirm contractual language and the DPA supplement. Jordan from Ops is on deck for the technical runbook.

Short operational answers for pilot (draft):
- Subprocessors: only our EU region compute and storage services + audited CDN partner (see roster in the playbook). No analytics providers will see production PII for the pilot.
- Transient cross-region processing: We can support a bounded window up to 48 hours for emergency failover scenarios (e.g., a regional outage) by default for sandbox accounts. For production-bound PII we recommend stricter limits. For Acme pilot we propose a 24-hour default window (pilot-configurable), after which requests are routed back or processed on-disk in-region.
- Evidence: attached playbook includes SOC2 control points mapping, sample audit log export (anonymized), and subprocessor list with effective dates.

Open clarifying questions:
1) Is Acme comfortable with a 24-hour temporary window for pilot telemetry and cache syncs, with an explicit prohibition on permanent storage outside EU for production PII?
2) Do you need KMS landing-zone evidence (we can provide a short KMS handshake diagram)?

Attachments: redwood-residency-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook excerpt)

If that looks ok I can have Kimberly produce a DPA supplement draft that captures the 24-hour pilot window and the subprocessors list.

—Markus
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency assurances for pilot and temporary-egress examples

Hi Priya / Markus — looping in formal language and one draft path for the DPA supplement.

Thanks for the redlines, Priya. We can accommodate a pilot-specific annex that: (a) enumerates the subprocessors active for the pilot, (b) limits transient cross-border processing to a defined hours window, and (c) commits to data-at-rest locality for production PII.

Key contract items we'd include in the supplement (draft items):
- Pilot transient window: 24 hours for caching/replication/kv-syncs unless Acme requests emergency extension via written ops authorization; any extension requires mutually agreed documented justification.
- Subprocessor roster: Redwood will provide roster with effective dates and SOC2 status; any additions during the pilot require 30 days notice and the option for Acme to request mitigation (e.g., IP allowlisting or operator scoping).
- KMS and key management: for EU-production datasets we offer customer-controlled keys via our KMS integration; we will provide the KMS handshake diagram and sample logs within the evidence pack.
- Audit evidence: sample anonymized audit logs, retention policy, and a point-in-time export for procurement review (we can provide one sample export for the pilot).

I've attached a DPA supplement draft (DPA_Supplement_Draft.docx) — it's intentionally conservative and focuses on pilot guardrails. Topics we still need to align on technically: 1) the exact telemetry subset permitted to cross-region during the window, and 2) whether operational metrics containing hashed identifiers are acceptable for EU->US analytical hops.

Priya — if acceptable I'll add a short acceptance checklist for procurement (DocuSign link below) and Marissa can coordinate timeline and rollout.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sandbox/packet/0a1b2c3d

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Markus — this is helpful, thank you. A couple quick responses from our side:
- The procurement team is comfortable with the 24-hour pilot window for non-production telemetry and cache syncs, provided we get the sample audit export and subprocessor roster before signing.
- We need the KMS handshake diagram and an example of the audit export by EOD next Tuesday so legal can clear the final DPA supplement.
- We'll proceed with the DocuSign packet for the pilot annex after we review the example materials.

Action items agreed:
1) Redwood to provide sample audit export (anonymized) and subprocessor roster — Markus/Jordan to own.
2) Redwood legal to deliver the DPA supplement in DocuSign — Kimberly to own.
3) Marissa to coordinate timing for pilot kickoff and procurement handoff (HubSpot deal attached).

Thanks — Priya
DPO, Acme Health
